title: The Weighing
subject: egyptian-mythology
author: Clueberry Desk
introduction: Ten entries from the paperwork of the next world.

entries.clue: Ibis-headed scribe who writes the verdict down
___ jar, the container for a removed organ
Green-skinned ruler presiding over the dead
Goddess whose single feather sets the standard
Small figure buried to do the labouring
Only major organ left inside the body, since it faced the scales
___ of Reeds, the destination worth hoping for

factCards.text: In the judgement scene of the Book of the Dead the heart is weighed against the feather of Maat, and Ammit waits to devour it should it prove heavier.
factCards.sourceTitle: Papyrus of Ani, British Museum EA10470

factCards.text: Embalmers removed the lungs, liver, stomach and intestines to canopic jars and discarded the brain, but left the heart in place as the seat of a person's character.
factCards.sourceTitle: British Museum, ancient Egyptian funerary practice

factCards.text: Ushabti figures were placed in tombs to perform agricultural work on the owner's behalf; some late burials held hundreds of them, one for each day of the year.
factCards.sourceTitle: Petrie Museum of Egyptian Archaeology; numbers vary widely by period
